messages:
customer-bob: Hey, after our IdP rotated certs around 10:30 UTC, users from corp.example.com get a 403 on SSO. It was fine earlier. Our middleware logs: "Invalid SAMLResponse: Signature verification failed". Any ideas?

support-alice: Sorry about that — we can triage. Is this for all users or a subset? Can you paste SP entityID + ACS and a decoded SAML error snippet (if available)?

customer-bob: All affected for now. entityID=https://app.customer.com/saml/sp, ACS=https://app.customer.com/saml/acs (no trailing slash). Decoded SAML trace shows: 
```
<samlp:Response>
  <!-- Signature validation error -->
  <ds:SignatureVerification>failed</ds:SignatureVerification>
</samlp:Response>
```

maya: Quick checklist: signature fail after idp rotation usually means our IdP metadata (signing cert) didn't update on Redwood side or the metadata fetch is broken. We poll metadata every 10m; if your metadata endpoint responds with a redirect to a login page (302) our fetch will not follow and refresh will fail.

sahil: Can you run a quick fetch from your side so we can see the headers? Try this (do NOT follow redirects):
```
curl -i https://idp.corp.example.com/metadata
```
Include output. If you see 302 -> /sso/login that's the culprit (metadata endpoint behind auth/CDN).

customer-bob: Ran that. Got 302 -> /portal/login (Set-Cookie: __sid=...). Looks like the metadata URL is on the same host as the interactive SSO and our CDN rewrites unauthenticated requests to the login page.

deploy-bot: metadata-refresh-job[svc/metadata-watcher] ran at 2026-03-17T10:40:00Z, result=error, message="unexpected 302". Next automatic retry in ~10m.

olivia: Two remediation paths: 1) Expose the metadata endpoint anonymously (recommended) so automatic polling can fetch new certs; or 2) as a short-term workaround, upload the new IdP signing cert manually in the Console: Console -> Security -> IdPs -> corp.example.com -> Upload signing cert. That will restore signature verification immediately.

henry: Also check for entityID normalization. If your IdP metadata lists entityID with a trailing slash (or with https vs http canonicalization), we might be matching a different entry. Make sure the SP entityID matches exactly what the IdP metadata says, or add the alias on the IdP side. Trailing slash mismatches are a common foot-gun.

support-alice: For our internal triage, please paste the exact metadata URL you expose and the curl output. We'll try a fetch from our backend too. Also include a base64-decoded SAMLResponse (if you can) and the exact time (UTC) of a failed login so we can correlate in logs.

customer-bob: Metadata URL: https://idp.corp.example.com/metadata. curl -i output:
```
HTTP/1.1 302 Found
Date: Wed, 17 Mar 2026 10:35:02 GMT
Server: nginx
Location: https://idp.corp.example.com/portal/login?rd=/metadata
Set-Cookie: __sid=xyz; Path=/; HttpOnly
Content-Length: 162
Content-Type: text/html; charset=UTF-8
```

sre-bot: note: our fetcher does not follow 302/301 for metadata endpoints by design (phishing/host-misconfiguration safety). If you must keep redirects, we can add a allowlist for this host but exposing raw metadata is preferred.

customer-bob: Understood. We can change CDN rule to exempt /metadata from auth. We'll do that now. In the meantime I uploaded the IdP signing cert manually to the Console per olivia's instructions.

maya: After manual upload, can you try a user login and paste the new SAMLResponse error (if any) or success? Also I'll trigger a force-refresh from our side: 
```
# internal admin command (run by infra)
rictl sso refresh --idp idp.corp.example.com --force
```

deploy-bot: trigger accepted by ops; job queued and running.

customer-bob: User login succeeded after manual cert upload. No more 403. We'll still open a ticket to fix metadata endpoint (make anonymous).

henry: Follow-up: once you allow anonymous metadata fetch, we should see the scheduled refresh pick up the new cert within 10m and you can remove the manual cert (or keep it as redundant). Also double-check NTP/time skew on your IdP—exp/NotBefore mismatches occasionally look like signature errors.

support-alice: Great — marking this thread as triaged. Actions: (1) customer will exempt /metadata from CDN auth; (2) ops executed force-refresh; (3) customer uploaded cert as temporary fix. We'll watch for one more successful automated refresh and then close. Please ping if anything reoccurs. :thumbsup:

customer-bob: Thanks all — will confirm when CDN rule is live. :thumbsup:

sre-bot: automated-scan: scheduled metadata poll succeeded at 2026-03-17T10:49:00Z after CDN change, status=200, cert-fingerprint=SHA256:AB:CD:EF:...

customer-bob: Confirmed — automated refresh picked up new cert and users are healthy. Closing from our side. :party:
